chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed we remain in winter for a day or two days without seeing any sun or star. So which day should we fast?' He said: 'Look at the day in which you fasted from the previous year, count five days, and fast on the fifth day.'

key_terms.الشِّتَاء: Winter — the season of extended cloud cover in many regions, making celestial moon-sighting impossible
key_terms.خَمْسَة أَيَّام: Five days — the prescribed interval to count forward from the previous year's fasting day
key_terms.شَمْس: Sun — used in jurisprudence for celestial observation to determine time and calendar
key_terms.نَجْم: Star — alongside the sun, used for timekeeping and direction
key_terms.نَصُوم: We fast (sawm) — refers specifically to the obligatory fast of Ramadan or recommended fasts

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about determining the day to fast when the sun and stars are not visible in winter?
ai.summary: Imran al-Za'farani posed a question to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about a practical difficulty of determining the correct day for fasting in winter when celestial bodies are obscured by clouds for extended periods. The Imam provided a practical jurisprudential method: recall the day one fasted in the previous year and count five days forward, fasting on the fifth day. This guidance reflects the Islamic lunar calendar's nature, where a lunar year is approximately 354 days — roughly 11 days shorter than the solar year. Counting five days accommodates the drift and accounts for the approximate shift of the moon's cycle relative to the season.
